title: fix(codex): preserve control characters in sandbox filenames
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex sandbox directory listing corrupts valid filenames containing tabs or newlines, and recursive copying then fails with “file not found.”

## User Impact

Directory listing and recursive copy preserve these filenames and their contents. Public RPC fields, sandbox permissions, symlink classification, and error messages stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell listing used tabs and newlines as separators even though both can appear in POSIX filenames. Its existing producer and parser now use NUL framing, which cannot occur in a basename. No configuration, persisted state, dependency, or public protocol changes are required.

## Evidence

- The added case failed against unchanged production through the actual WebSocket RPC and shell bridge, showing both corrupted listing and recursive-copy failure.
- All 34 tests pass across the real bridge composition, filesystem RPC, and streaming files.
- The regression extends the existing fixture without another server boot, sleeps, or polling. `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.fs-bridge-composition.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed in 75.08s process wall; its single composed test took 3.996s on the overloaded fallback host.
- Both import-cycle checkers report zero; independent Codex review is clean through P2. No imports or public SDK declarations change.
- Personally checked the upstream Codex filename contract and local filesystem implementation at `8f38d5a877da8c5c2c0b5158e72bb5f2290a3157` (`exec-server-protocol/src/protocol.rs` and `exec-server/src/local_file_system.rs`).

Remote capacity had already failed after bounded retries exceeding ten minutes. These focused checks used the authorized `nice -n 15` local fallback, one heavy command at a time. Exact-head [CI run 36847369353](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36847369353) passed. Its Codex extension selection passed all 55 tests in six files; the real bridge regression took 0.902s on Linux (selection process wall 63.94s). The PR merged as `1b5db5e90b82e7122bc4315b01e4507ac38f2a35`, verified as an ancestor of current main with identical changed-file contents.
